title: Shareef Ahmad v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J. & Dinesh Pathak, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of without deciding merits; petitioner to file a representation within three weeks for a reasoned speaking order on final assessment after hearing, preferably within four weeks of receipt; no coercive action on the citation dated 18.11.2020 for six weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier; no benefit if the representation is not filed
headnote: Failure to object to a provisional assessment, including silence after the time allowed for reply, does not convert that provisional figure into a final assessment. Applying Shishir Jain, the Division Bench held that the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the provisionally assessed amount unless a final assessment is made after an opportunity of hearing and a copy of that order is supplied. Treating the provisional amount as final without a hearing is dehors Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 — Clause 8.1 being the theft procedure of inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment — and violates natural justice. Without entering the merits, the Court directed a representation within three weeks for a speaking final assessment after hearing, stayed coercive action on the 18 November 2020 recovery citation for six weeks or until that decision, and withheld the benefit of the order if the representation is not filed. The citation was not quashed.
facts:
Shareef Ahmad filed Writ-C No. 26825 of 2020 in the Allahabad High Court against the State of U.P. and three others, seeking to quash a recovery citation dated 18 November 2020 issued by respondent no. 4 for Rs. 1,94,392. He said he held a valid electricity connection and paid bills regularly. On 11 September 2019 a checking authority inspected his premises and reported theft of electricity. An FIR was lodged on 25 September 2019 under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003. A provisional assessment notice dated 31 October 2019 under Section 126 was sent by registered post; he filed no objection. He contended that no final assessment was thereafter served and that he was given no hearing before recovery.

Counsel for the Power Corporation (respondent nos. 2 and 3) could not show that if a person fails to reply to a provisional assessment within 15 days, that provisional assessment is treated as the final assessment. Naheed Ara Moonis and Dinesh Pathak, JJ. disposed of the writ on 18 January 2021.

reusable_constructions.construction: Failure to object to a provisional assessment, including silence after the period allowed for reply, does not convert that provisional assessment into a final assessment.
A consumer cannot be compelled to deposit a provisionally assessed amount unless a final assessment is made after an opportunity of hearing and a copy of that order is supplied.

Treating the amount in a provisional theft assessment as the final assessment without a hearing is dehors Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 8.1 of the Supply Code, 2005, and violates natural justice.
Clause 8.1 of the Supply Code, 2005 is the procedure for inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment in a case of theft of electricity.

holding_units.topic: theft assessment — silence on the provisional notice does not make it final; hearing and a served final order are required before recovery
holding_units.question: May a licensee recover a theft demand by treating a provisional assessment as final because the consumer did not object within 15 days, without a hearing and without supplying a copy of a final order?
holding_units.holding: No. The Power Corporation could not show that failure to reply within 15 days converts the provisional assessment into a final one. The Court was not convinced that absence of objection has that effect. Clause 8.1, read with Section 126, requires inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and a final assessment in theft cases. Treating the provisional amount as the final assessment without a hearing, and compelling deposit without supplying a copy of the final order, is dehors those provisions and violates natural justice. Applying Shishir Jain paragraph 16, the petitioner could not be compelled to deposit on the provisional figure. Without deciding merits, he was directed to file a representation within three weeks for a reasoned speaking final assessment after hearing, preferably within four weeks of receipt. Coercive action on the 18.11.2020 citation is stayed for six weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier; if he does not file the representation, he gets no benefit of the order.
holding_units.qualifier: The 18.11.2020 citation was not quashed. Petitioner invoked Section 126(3) and Clause 8.1; the Court's holding is framed as Section 126 and Clause 8.1.
holding_units.flag: Unnumbered 18.1.2021 order; paras are sequential blocks after the cause-title (1 heard; 2 reliefs; 3 inspection 11.09.2019, FIR 25.09.2019 s.135, provisional 31.10.2019 s.126 by registered post, no objection, citation 18.11.2020 for Rs. 1,94,392; 4 no hearing, s.126(3) and Clause 8.1, Shishir Jain; 5 licensee could not show 15-day silence deems the provisional final; Court not convinced; 6 Shishir Jain para 16 quoted; 7 procedure dehors s.126 and Clause 8.1, Clause 8.1 described as the theft path, treating provisional as final without hearing violates natural justice; 8 representation directed without entering merits; 9 stay of recovery; 10 no benefit if representation not filed). FIR under s.135; assessment notice under s.126; Court applied both s.126 and Clause 8.1 without electing between unauthorised use and theft. Catalog hits on Clauses 4.3, 4.35–4.39 and 8.14 are false positives.

holding_units.topic: no compulsion to deposit a provisional Section 126 assessment until a final assessment after hearing
holding_units.question: Does want of an objection within 15 days of a Section 126 provisional assessment authorise recovery of that figure as a concluded final assessment?
holding_units.holding: No. Licensee's counsel could not show that failure to reply within 15 days treats the provisional assessment as final. Following Shishir Jain paragraph 16, without a final assessment after considering the objection and giving an opportunity of hearing, and without supplying a copy of that order, the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the provisional amount. The procedure adopted was held dehors Section 126. Recovery was not allowed to proceed as a concluded final assessment; it was stayed pending a speaking decision on a representation after hearing.
holding_units.qualifier: Petitioner invoked Section 126(3); the Court's own holding is framed as Section 126. The citation was not quashed.

principle_tags.application: The 31.10.2019 Section 126 provisional notice was treated as the concluded demand because the petitioner did not object. The Court rejected that deemed-final step and would not let the 18.11.2020 citation recover the provisional figure as a final assessment.

authorities.name: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and another
authorities.proposition: If there is no final assessment, the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the amount of the provisional assessment; without a final assessment after considering the objection and giving an opportunity of hearing, notices demanding that amount are unsustainable (para 16).
